FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Electrical Appliances Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council. Electric without warming plates, warming trays and similar devices are used for keeping the food warm the risk of its getting burnt. covers the general, safety and constructional requirements of warming plates.

The standard

This standard is to be read in conjunction with IS 302 : 1979 `General and safety requirements for household and similar electrical appliances (fifth revision )`. For the sake of convenience, the clauses of this standard correspond to those of IS 302 : 1979 which are applicable ( which means that relevant provisions of the clause shall apply, or not applicable and the sub-clauses or portions thereof which are not applicable are indicated as under: a) In case of a clause where it is applicable or not applicable, clause of IS 302 : 1979 is applicable/not applicable'. b) In case of a sub-clause or part thereof `Not applicable'* Wherever under: a sub-clause of IS 302 : 1979 is to be replaced followed existing by the new text'. provisions of a sub-clause of IS 302 : 1979 has been indicated matter'. as the wording used is `This

by a new text, it has been indicated

as

`Replacement Any addition under: `Addition

to the -

followed by the text of the additional

Clauses/tables which are additional to those of IS 302 : 1979 are numbered starting from 101 and additional sub-clauses are numbered with the main clauses number followed by 101, 102, etc, for example, 7.101. Additional annexes have been numbered starting from AA. the provisions of Should however any deviation the latter shall apply. While preparing this standard, exist between IS 302 : 1979 and this standard, assistance has been derived from the following

publications:

IEC Pub 335-l ( 1976 ) Safety of household and similar electrical appliances: Part 1 General requirements, issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. IEC Publication 335-2-12 ( 1987 ) Safety of household and similar electric appliances: Part 2 Particular requirements for warming plates and similar appliances, issued by the International Electrotechnical Commission. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised )`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

WARMING PLATES 1 SCOPE Clause 1 of IS 302 : 1979 is applicable as follows: except

SPECIFICATION

1.1Replacement
This standard covers the electric warming plates, warming trays and similar devices for keeping the food or food vessels warm for household and similar purposes.
NOTE - Appliances not intended for normal household use but which nevertheless may be a souice of danger to the public such as the appliances intended to be used by persons in canteens and restaurants are within the scope of this standard.

Additional Sub-clauses: 2.101 Warming Plate - An appliance having an internally electrically heated surface on which vessels or foods are intended to be placed in order to be held at or brought to a temperature suitable for serving. 2.102 Warming Tray - A warming plate intended to receive a variety of different vessels on the heated surface. 2.103 Particularized Warming Plate - A warming plate intended to receive only certain food or beverage serving vessels which may either be provided with the plate or specified in the instructions. 3 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS except

Clause 18 of IS 302 : 1979 is applicable as follows:
18.1 Replacement

Appliances shall be so constructed that in normal use there will be no electrical or mechanical failure that might impair compliance with this standard. The insulation shall not be damaged and contacts and connections shall not work loose after the endurance test.
18.2 Replacement

Compliance is checked by the tests of 19.2 and if necessary by the test of 19.3 followed by the test of 19.4 for appliances provided with a control which limits the temperature during the test of 11 and by the test of 19.101 for appliances. Paras 5 and 6 Not applicable. 19.5 to 19.10 Not applicable. Additional sub-clause:

The appliances shall be connected to the supply with a vessel as specified in 2.29 on the heating element, and such that the input is l-10 times of maximum rated input which shall be maintained through out the test. The endurance test shall consist of 500 cycles. each cycle comprising two hours connection to supply and two hour disconnection. NOTE `- For the purpose of endurance test on appliances, the operating time for the tests in 11,12 and 13 is included. During the test 20 spillages each consisting of 150 ml of 0.5 percent solution of sodium chloride in distilled water at room temperature shall be projected over the plate in a period of one minute, subject to the condition that: there shall not be more than 4 a> in any 100 cycles, and these spillages shall be equally spaced as nearly as possible over the time involved; and spillages shall be made on the plate in hot and cold states, that is, 15 minutes after commencement of an `on' period and 15 minutes after the commencement of an `off' period.

19.101 The appliances are operated for 7 h at a supply voltage such that the input is equal to rated input, without a vessel or other object on the heated surface, this surface being however, completely covered with a double layer of cotton gauze as specified in Appendix A4 and with a hair?felt pad having a thickness of 25 mm. If a thermostat starts to cycle, the test is repeated with only one-third of the heated surface furthest from the temperature sensing element covered. During the test, the appliance shall not emit flames or molten metal and there shall be no flowing of combustible material. If, after the test, the appliance appears to be usable, it shall withstand the test of 16.2. For appliances provided with heating elements with appreciable positive temperature coefficient of resistance, the supply voltage is determined as specified in 4.12. 20 STABILITY HAZARDS AND MECHANICAL except

b) alternative

Five minutes after each spillage, the appliance shall be subjected to a mechanical shock test by allowing a hardened steel bell of 75 mm in diameter to drop freely six times from a height of 150 mm on to a 3 mm thick steel plate ( which shall be of a sufficient area to cover the appliance placed over the hot-plate. Care shall be taken that the ball falls on different parts of the surface of the steel plate, these parts being selected at random. 2 At the end of the endurance test, the appliance shall be checked for compliance with 18.5 of .e IS 302 : 1979.

A vessel having a bottom of copper or aluminium, which is a flat over a distance of 12 f 1 cm and has edges rounded with a radius of at least 1 cm: and uniformly filled with sand or shot to a total mass of 1.8 kg, is dropped flat, from a height of 15 cm, onto the surface of glass, ceramic or similar brittle material. The appliance is then operated at rated voltage or at the upper limit of the rated voltage range, until steady conditions are established. Immediately afterwards, a cotton sheet having dimensions of 40 cm x 40 cm and a mass between 140 g/m2 and 175 g/ma in the dry condition, which is soaked with cold water and then folded four times so as to form a pad having dimensions of approximately 10 cm x 10 cm, is applied to the most unfavourable part of the surface of glass, ceramic or similar brittle material. After these tests, the surface shall not be broken and shall show no crack visible to the naked eye, and the appliance shall withstand the test of 16.2. 23 INTERNAL WIRING .except Clause 23 of IS 302 * 1979 is applicable as follows: 23.4 and 23.7 Not applicable. 24 COMPONENTS Clause 24 of IS 302 : 1979 is applicable as follows: 24.4 to 24.10 Not applicable. 25 SUPPLY CONNECTION AND EXTERNAL FLEXIBLE CABLES AND CORDS Clause 25 of IS 302 : 1979 is applicable as follows: 25.1 Replacement Appliances shall be provided with a power inlet for supply card or an appliance connection to the ~ppply., Compliance is checked by inspection. 1

The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
